mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced discount rates for equity cash flows.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to recession fears.
failure_condition: The SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1000 and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 6.0%, it indicates a strong housing market and labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (HOUST>1000 AND UNRATE<6.0%) is met in more than 40% of cases but the 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% qoq and unemployment rate below 5.0%), S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive due to sustained economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% qoq and UNRATE < 5.0%) is met in more than 40% of cases but the 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: An industrial production (INDPRO) level above 102.0 indicates strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns due to elevated corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The INDPRO level above 102.0 is met in more than 40% of cases but the 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: A higher Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which erodes real earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 60-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeds 100.0 thousand persons and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 6.0%, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (PAYEMS growth > 100.0 and UNRATE < 6.0%) is met in more than 40% of cases but the 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS above 2.0% and CPIAUCSL growth above 2.0% qoq), S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: The monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS>2.0% and CPIAUCSL growth>2.0% qoq) is met in more than 40% of cases but the 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of those cases.
